mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a -2% y/y drop in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as a 0.5 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points in the month following the UNRATE trigger, indicating the labor market weakness is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, defined as the 10-year Treasury yield falling below the 2-year yield, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The yield curve steepens by > 20 basis points within 3 months of inverting, indicating the tightening cycle is over.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts and falling mortgage rates signals increased housing demand that will boost related sectors and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The NAHB Housing Market Index falls by > 10 points in the month following the signal, indicating builder pessimism that will negate the positive demand signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in payroll employment, defined as a 200,000 decline in the PAYEMS series over the past month, signals a sudden labor market shock that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall by > 20,000 in the week following the PAYEMS drop, indicating the labor market shock is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the CPI inflation rate, defined as a 0.5 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a wage-price spiral that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker rises by < 0.5 percentage points in the quarter following the CPI trigger, indicating the inflation is not yet embedded in wages.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising retail sales and falling unemployment signals a strengthening consumer sector that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real personal income (excluding transfers) falls by > 0.5% in the month following the signal, indicating the consumer strength is not sustainable.
